title: Revisit the win32-x64 add-on load-failure carve-out when Bun fixes the load (DEC-80 follow-up)
description:
Filed on DEC-80 (operator choice A, recorded in opum-agent `.quest/planning.json`, accepted; relayed as ODOC-OP-2026-09-30-09, seq 74, 13:25:41Z), which required this follow-up as its own third item: "file a follow-up to revisit the carve-out once Bun fixes the load".

WHAT THE CARVE-OUT IS. Under bun 1.4.2 the Ladybug add-on cannot load on win32-x64: the DLL's initialization routine fails (`LoadLibrary failed: A dynamic link library (DLL) initialization routine failed.`), identically through the interpreter's `require` and through a direct `process.dlopen` (diag run 36706380224). The same runner image (win25-vs2026/20260922.246) and byte-identical add-on bytes load cleanly under bun 1.3.14 at v0.11.0, so the runtime transition is the variable -- see LCLI-657 for the full measurement, including quest-cli's finding that `process.dlopen`'s own Windows load call is unchanged across 1.3.14/1.4.0/1.4.2 and that the module loader was rewritten Zig to Rust in 1.4.0.

Because Windows is reference-fallback-only by construction (package-qualification.ts:392/:397 and the report validator's equality at :262; docs/reference/architecture.md:386; docs/reference/tech-stack.md:361), the probe is a characterization step whose subject the product does not use on Windows, and the artifact-level steps -- pack, install, global launcher, relocated executable, smoke, uninstall, audit -- all pass on win32-x64 under 1.4.2 (diag run 36706817656, a deliberately relaxed gate, evidence about the artifact and NOT a qualification). The amendment therefore accepts ONE shape: a win32-x64 probe verdict of `unavailable` whose recorded stderr carries exactly `WINDOWS_ADDON_LOAD_FAILURE_MESSAGE` as the child's own first line, with the message recorded in the report; every other shape stays refused, enforced by `windowsAddonLoadFailurePolicyHolds` and asserted at the validator.

WHY THIS TASK EXISTS RATHER THAN A COMMENT. The amendment knowingly costs something: the Windows probe no longer discriminates this class, so a FUTURE Windows regression that also presents as a load failure would be accepted silently. That cost is only acceptable while the load is genuinely broken upstream. This task is the trigger that removes it -- and its AC1 makes the trigger a MEASUREMENT rather than a date, a changelog line or a release note, because the entire episode began with a runtime change whose release notes said nothing about add-on loading.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The win32-x64 acceptance is restored to refusing every load outcome -- or its continuation is re-justified with a fresh measurement -- on the evidence of a qualification run in which the probe child imports the Ladybug add-on cleanly under the pinned runtime, never on a Bun changelog or release note.

If the load is fixed, WINDOWS_ADDON_LOAD_FAILURE_MESSAGE, the classifier's addon-load-unavailable arm, the report's addonLoadFailureMessage field and windowsAddonLoadFailurePolicyHolds all go in one change, with the fixture that pins each refusal shape removed alongside them.
